title: Month 27
subtitle: Three words together, and a tricycle is the next thing.

baby.development: Your child says three words together, can jump with both feet, and can walk up stairs alternating feet with a hand held. They are starting to use a spoon and fork together.

you.body: If you are carrying a twenty-seven-month-old, your back has been doing this for over two years. A physio visit is not an indulgence.
you.mind: Twenty-seven months is when the child starts to tell you what happened. The stories are short and mostly about the dog, and they are the beginning of narrative.

coreActions.title: Get a tricycle, or a balance bike
coreActions.why: Pedalling is a coordination skill that comes before riding, and a balance bike teaches the balance that a tricycle does not.
coreActions.detail: A tricycle with pedals is the traditional first step. A balance bike skips the pedals and teaches balance first, which most children find easier. Either is fine. A helmet from the first ride, every time.

coreActions.title: Let them use a fork, and expect it to be slow
coreActions.why: Using a fork is a fine-motor skill that takes a year, and it only develops if the child is allowed to do it.
coreActions.detail: A small fork with rounded tines. Stab a piece and hand it over to start. Expect the food to be dropped and the meal to take longer. Do not take the fork away to finish faster.

coreActions.title: A helmet from the first ride
coreActions.why: A helmet that is not worn from the first ride is a helmet that is fought over at four.
coreActions.detail: Fit it so it sits level, two fingers above the eyebrow, with the strap snug under the chin. Wear one yourself. A child who sees a helmet on every ride does not question it.

alsoKnow.title: Ask what happened, not what they did
alsoKnow.body: A child who is asked what happened at the park will tell a story. A child who is asked if they had fun will say yes. The first builds language, the second does not.

alsoKnow.title: The nap is still needed
alsoKnow.body: Most two-year-olds still need one nap of one to two hours. Dropping it early makes the evening worse, not better.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fall from a bike or a height, or a head injury with vomiting or unusual sleepiness
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
